items.title: Somalia's Federal Member States Aren't Defending Sovereignty — They're Defending Their Patrons - No One in This Fight Is Neutral
items.description: Puntland is furious at Türkiye. Jubaland is furious at Türkiye. Both have spent the past five weeks accusing Ankara of killing their own people. Neither is in a position to make that accusation as a matter of principle. Puntland's ports are run by the UAE. Jubaland's survival for over a decade has depended on Kenya. The one Somali federal member state that tried to stand apart from any foreign patron — South West State — was crushed by federal troops within 48 hours in March. items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.
items.titleIt: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu

items.description: The group that arrived in Mogadishu reportedly comprised 25 men and 25 women. items.title: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free
items.description: A death sentence in Somalia isn't final until the president signs it. Increasingly, none of them do.   That piece traced how Ahmed Shire Hussein, a Somali National Army soldier, was executed on camera near El Baraf for the crime of his father's clan — one entry in a pattern of hit squads, informant networks, and a tribal shield strong enough that a court willing to execute Al-Shabaab fighters would not touch a killer protected by his own sub-clan. Why does almost no one ever pay for it? This is the answer: what decides whether the state acts is the relative political power of the clans in
items.titleIt: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free

items.title: Somalia: Blood, Blades, and Broken Streets: Inside the Terror Colonizing Mogadishu
items.description: Speaking after his son's funeral at Muuse Boqor Mosque the following day, veteran journalist Maxamed Cumar Baakaay put words to what the killing meant: "Allah gave me my son, and now Allah has taken him back. I praise Him. We have survived so many historic atrocities here in Mogadishu, only for me to lose my boy to the blades of the Ciyaal Weero." Family members say police have since detained several suspects, though authorities have not issued an official statement confirming the arrests. A journalist mourning his university-bound son has shattered the illusion of security in central Mogadish
items.titleIt: Somalia: Blood, Blades, and Broken Streets: Inside the Terror Colonizing Mogadishu

items.title: The Anatomy of a Blood Debt: How Clan Revenge Killings are Fracturing Somalia's Frontlines
items.description: Before he was executed, a chilling video captured his final moments. Stranded and defenseless, Hussein looked directly at his armed captors and uttered a devastating plea: "Abtiyaalow, ha i dilina" ("Maternal uncles, do not kill me"). The phrase was not just a desperate cry for mercy — according to clan elders and opposition figures interviewed for this piece, it reflected a specific and devastating reality. items.titleIt: The Anatomy of a Blood Debt: How Clan Revenge Killings are Fracturing Somalia's Frontlines

items.title: AFRICOM Conducts Airstrike Against al-Shabaab in Somalia
items.description: According to AFRICOM, the strike took place approximately 175 kilometers west of Mogadishu as part of ongoing joint efforts to weaken al-Shabaab's operational capabilities. AFRICOM said it continues to work alongside the Somali federal government and Somali Armed Forces to degrade the militant group's ability to threaten U.S. forces and American citizens abroad. The command did not disclose specific details about the units or military assets involved, citing operational security concerns. The strike comes as Somali and international forces continue military operations against al-Shabaab, which
items.titleIt: AFRICOM Conducts Airstrike Against al-Shabaab in Somalia

items.title: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen
items.description: As we have learnt from two individuals affected, Swiss police authorities use an enormous amount of violence during forced deportations. From the perspective of lawyers and Swiss human rights organisations, the authorities are thereby committing massive violations of Swiss and international law. Furthermore, in at least two cases, they have put the lives of those affected at serious risk. Augenauf shares this assessment and has informed the relevant authorities (including the commander of the Zurich cantonal police and the National Commission for the Prevention of Torture, NKVF). Bot
items.titleIt: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: 'Gunfire everywhere': Displaced Yemenis describe terrifying journey to Djibouti
items.description: Displaced Yemenis who fled to Djibouti have been describing the fighting that forced them to leave. At least 100,000 people have left Yemen since the start of September as Iran-backed Houthi rebels advanced on the coast, seizing control of the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait.
